rows.text: You have almost certainly used artificial intelligence today.
A search suggestion. An autocorrected word. A recommended video.
But most people could not explain what it actually does.
In the next few minutes, you will be able to.
The chatbots and writing assistants you hear about are built on something called a large language model.
Its core job is easy to state. Given some text, predict the text that is most likely to come next.
Take the sentence: the capital of France is. The model assigns a probability to every possible next word.
Paris gets a very high one. Most other words get almost none.
It picks one, adds it to the text, and repeats. One word at a time, that is how a full answer gets written.
More precisely, it works in small pieces called tokens, which are often parts of words rather than whole words.
